fullName.description: Full name, used only when a new user is created. Apple provides the name on the first authorization only, so send it then; null or ignored afterwards

nonce.description: The raw nonce this sign-in started with. The client sends its SHA-256 hex to Apple and the raw value here; the server checks the token's `nonce` claim against it, so a captured token cannot be replayed from another session

AuditLogResponse.description: One audit log entry: a write action and whether it succeeded

action.description: Action, e.g. CREATE, DELETE, SUSPEND, FORCE_CLOSE

details.description: Extra context: the suspend reason (as given) or the new roles (sorted, comma-separated, e.g. `admin,user`); null when none

errorMessage.description: Error message of a failed action; null on success

httpMethod.description: HTTP method; null for failed actions

requestUri.description: Request path; null for failed actions

resourceId.description: Affected resource ID; null when not recorded

resourceType.description: Resource type, e.g. VOTE, COMMENT, USER

success.description: Whether the action succeeded

userAgent.description: Client User-Agent; null for failed actions

userId.description: Acting user's ID; null for unauthenticated requests

username.description: Acting user's username at the time; null when unknown (entries before 2026-10-23 hold the email)

AuthResponse.description: Response after a successful login, signup or token refresh

isNewUser.description: True when this sign-in is the account's first (it was just created), so the client can show signup wording. Null on POST /api/auth/refresh

refreshToken.description: Opaque refresh token, valid for 30 days by default. Use it with POST /api/auth/refresh when the access token expires. Single-use: every refresh returns a new one that replaces it

token.description: JWT access token; send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Valid for 15 minutes by default

optionId.description: Chosen option; null once an Anonymous Ballot of an Ended Poll was sealed

CommentDto.description: A Comment (top-level) or a Reply (parentId set) on a Poll

author.description: Username of the author. Null only on a deleted placeholder (`deleted` = true)

authorAvatarUrl.description: Avatar of the author as `bot:<kind>` (the bot cast). Older accounts may hold an image URL; null if never set, and on a deleted placeholder (`deleted` = true)

deleted.description: True for a deleted top-level Comment kept as a placeholder because it still has Replies; userId, author, authorAvatarUrl and text are then null. Deleted Comments without Replies are not returned at all

edited.description: True once the text was edited after posting (updatedAt is after createdAt). Always false for a deleted placeholder

likedByCurrentUser.description: Whether the signed-in user liked this Comment. Always false when the request is not authenticated

info.description:
REST API of Vomatt, a social polling platform.

**Envelope**: every response is `{ success, data, message, errorCode, error }`. On success `data` holds the payload; on failure `success=false` and `data` is normally null.

**Auth**: `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` (JWT). Obtain tokens via `/api/auth/**`; 401 `auth.token.expired` means refresh, `auth.token.invalid` means sign in again.

**Errors**: branch on `errorCode` (lowercase dotted, e.g. `vote.not_found`), never on `message`. Filter-level 401/403/429 use the same body. 429 carries a `Retry-After` header (seconds), except when the rate limiter itself is unavailable.

**Pagination**: list endpoints return `{ items, nextCursor }`; pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor`. `limit` defaults to 20 and is clamped to 1..50.

**i18n**: send `Accept-Language` (`zh-TW` default, `en`) to localize `message`.

Conventions, flows and glossary: `docs/frontend/README.md` in the repository.

- 401 `auth.suspicious_login`: a spent token was reused after the grace window; the session it belonged to is now signed out

**Auth**: public
**Precondition**: none; the same endpoint serves login and signup (the server picks which by whether the email is registered)
**Behavior**: generates a 6-digit OTP, stores it with a TTL (default 180 s) and emails it. The email is lower-cased and trimmed; a Gmail address (gmail.com / googlemail.com) also loses its +tag and dots and moves to gmail.com. The admin console signs in with `POST /api/auth/admin/send-otp` instead
**Side effects**: sends an email; replaces any previous OTP for this address. A resend is refused during the cooldown (default 180 s), and at most 20 OTPs are sent to one address per UTC day
**Errors**:
- 400 `auth.identifier.required`: `email` is missing or blank
- 400 `auth.otp.resend_cooldown`: an OTP was sent too recently; the message states the seconds left
- 400 `auth.email.send_failed`: the email provider rejected the message; the OTP is dropped and a resend is allowed after 30 s
- 401 `auth.otp.too_many_attempts`: this email is locked for the caller's IP after 3 wrong codes (5 minutes, doubling on each further lockout, up to 24 hours); other IPs are not affected
- 429 `auth.otp.daily_limit`: 20 OTPs were already sent to this address today (UTC)

**Auth**: public
**Precondition**: an OTP was sent to this email via `POST /api/auth/send-otp` and has not expired
**Behavior**: consumes the OTP and returns an access token and refresh token. Creates the user if the email is new (signup), otherwise signs the existing user in; `isNewUser` tells which, so the client needs no separate registration check. The tokens never grant the admin role, even for an admin account: the admin console signs in with `POST /api/auth/admin/verify-otp`
**Side effects**: the OTP is consumed on success; a new user (with a random bot avatar) is created and a welcome email sent on signup; `lastLoginAt` is updated. Wrong codes are counted per email and client IP; resending does not reset the count. The 3rd wrong code locks this email for the caller's IP for 5 minutes, doubling on each further lockout (10, 20, 40 minutes...) up to 24 hours; the doubling is forgotten 24 hours after the last lock ends, and a successful sign-in from that IP resets it. While locked, sending or verifying an OTP from that IP is refused; other IPs are not affected and the OTP stays valid. One OTP allows 10 guesses in total across all IPs; after the 10th wrong guess it no longer verifies and a new OTP can be requested only after 15 minutes
**Errors**:
- 400 `auth.identifier.required`: `email` is missing or blank
- 401 `auth.otp.invalid_or_expired`: no OTP exists for this email (never sent, expired, already used, or its 10 guesses are used up)
- 401 `auth.invalid_otp`: the code is wrong
- 401 `auth.otp.too_many_attempts`: 3rd wrong code, or this identifier is locked for the caller's IP (even a correct code is refused until the lock ends)
- 403 `auth.account_banned`: the user is suspended (`active=false`)

**Auth**: required
**Precondition**: none
**Behavior**: the caller's notifications, newest `createdAt` first, cursor-paged. They are not stored but derived from Polls, Invitations, follows and Comments when read, so an item disappears when what it is about goes away (a Comment deleted, a follow undone, a Poll Deleted). Kinds:
- RESULT: a Poll the caller owns, holds a Ballot in or is an Invitee of has Ended (end time passed, Closed, or every Invitee voted). A Participant who made a Retraction and is not an Invitee gets none
- CANCELLED: an Invite-only Poll the caller is an Invitee of was Cancelled before it opened (only Polls Cancelled before 2026-10-14; a Scheduled Poll is now Deleted, which notifies nobody)
- INVITATION: the caller is an Invitee of a Scheduled or Open Invite-only Poll; listed until the Poll Ends, when its RESULT takes over. Being removed and invited again is a new, unread INVITATION
- FOLLOWED: someone followed the caller (one item per follower; group them in the UI)
- COMMENT: someone else commented on or replied under the caller's Poll, or replied to the caller's Comment, on a Poll the caller can see; not a Reply in a thread started by a user the caller blocked (the Comment lists hide that thread)
- CLOSING_SOON: an Open Poll ends within 24 hours and the caller holds no Ballot in it, if the caller is its Invitee, or it is a Public Poll of a user the caller follows. Gone once the caller casts a Ballot or the Poll Ends. Off by default
Kinds switched off in the caller's preferences are left out (FOLLOWED cannot be switched off). Nothing from a suspended user, a user the caller blocked or a user who blocked the caller is listed, nor anything about a Poll whose owner blocked the caller. `poll` never carries per-option counts, its outcome (`winningOptionIds`, `winningOptionLabels`, `tie`) stays null until the Poll has Ended, and `actor` is never a voter, so Sealed results and Anonymous Ballots stay hidden. Each item carries what a row needs: the caller's Selection (`poll.myOptionId`), the caller's follows with the actor both ways (`actor.isFollowing`, `actor.followsYou`), and for a Reply the Comment it is under (`comment.parentId`). An item can appear or vanish behind a cursor (a follow, a block); de-duplicate by `id`.

post.description:
**Auth**: required
**Precondition**: none
**Behavior**: creates a Poll owned by the caller. With no `startTime` (or a past one) the Poll is Open immediately; a future `startTime` makes it Scheduled until that time. `voterVisibility` defaults to OWNER (the deprecated `anonymous: true` without `voterVisibility` means NOBODY); `audience` defaults to PUBLIC. An UNLISTED Poll is reachable only through its link: it stays out of Feed / Explore / Search and the owner's profile, and is listed only in My Polls. An INVITE_ONLY Poll is reachable only by its owner and its Invitees: the users in `inviteeIds` and the addresses in `inviteeEmails` (duplicates and the owner's own ID / address are ignored; more can be added later); everyone else gets 404 `vote.not_found`. An address is always listed as entered, whether or not it belongs to an account; an active account's user gets access right away, any other address once someone verifies it at sign-up / sign-in. `inviteListIds` invites the current members of the caller's Invite Lists: members added by ID join `inviteeIds` (suspended ones are skipped) and members added by email join `inviteeEmails` by their stored address; later Invite List changes never touch the Poll.
**Side effects**: usage count of each attached tag +1 for a PUBLIC Poll (UNLISTED and INVITE_ONLY Polls are not counted); each Invitee tied to a user gets an unread Invitation notification (unread count, `unread` on My Polls `status=open`); each new email Invitee is sent an invitation email linking to the Poll (only when email is enabled) (at most once per address per Poll, even after removing and re-adding it, and at most `EMAIL_INVITATION_DAILY_LIMIT` (default 200) per owner per day; over the limit the Invitee is still added and only the email is skipped) and gets the Invitation notification once tied to a user; the creation is audit-logged.
**Errors**:

        - 400 `vote.multiple.not_allowed`: `allowMultipleChoices` is true

        - 400 `vote.end_time.before_start`: `endTime` is not after `startTime`

- 404 `invite_list.not_found`: one of `inviteListIds` does not exist or belongs to someone else

**Auth**: required (owner only)
**Precondition**: the Poll is INVITE_ONLY and Scheduled or Open (Invitees can still be added after it opened)
**Behavior**: adds the users and email addresses as Invitees, so they can see the Poll, cast a Ballot and Comment, and find it in My Polls. An address is always listed as entered, whether or not it belongs to an account; an active account's user gets access right away, any other address once someone verifies it at sign-up / sign-in. `inviteListIds` invites the current members of the caller's Invite Lists: members added by ID join `userIds` (suspended ones are skipped) and members added by email join `emails` by their stored address; later Invite List changes never touch the Poll. - 400 `vote.ended`: the Poll has Ended

**Auth**: required
**Precondition**: the Poll is Open (not Scheduled, not Ended)
**Behavior**: records the caller's Ballot with exactly one Selection. If the caller already holds a Ballot it is replaced by the new one (change of mind); casting the same option again only updates `anonymous`. `anonymous: true` makes it an Anonymous Ballot, left out of `GET /api/votes/{voteId}/voters` whatever the Poll's Voter Visibility; an omitted or `null` `anonymous` keeps the current Ballot's flag, and a first Ballot uses the caller's `anonymousBallotByDefault` (false until set).
